standard.title: Insulating Varnishes Containing Solvents — Specification (First Revision) (विद्युतरोधी विलायकयुक्त वार्निश — विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
standard.sector: Electrotechnical / Solid Electrical Insulating Materials and Insulation Systems

sectional_committee.name: Solid Electrical Insulating Materials and Insulation Systems Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard series prescribes definitions, general requirements, testing methodologies, and individual material specifications for solvent-containing electrical insulating varnishes used for impregnating, finishing, and coating electrical windings, transformers, coils, and electric motors. Part 3, Section 2 specifically covers physical, mechanical, and electrical requirements for hot curing impregnating varnishes across thermal classes 130 to 220.

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. However, under public utility contracts (such as state electricity boards—JVVNL, KSEB—and central railway specifications), raw insulating varnishes supplied for winding repair and motor manufacture must be certified to comply with IS 10026 and carry corresponding batch test records.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, solid contents, viscosity flow times, or breakdown voltages must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Measured by heating a 1.5 g liquid specimen at 130°C or 150°C for 2 hours to calculate active dry resin percentage, which must typically range between 45% and 55% to prevent excessive solvent loss.
A critical test for impregnating varnishes. Evaluates if the varnish inside a deep winding cavity will cure fully into a solid, bubble-free mass when baked at 120°C for 10 hours.

The cured varnish film must exhibit high dielectric strength, withstanding voltages exceeding 100 kV/mm under ambient conditions, and retaining high dielectric protection after wet conditioning or water immersion.
The cured film must maintain a volume resistivity exceeding 10^15 Ohm-cm under standard ambient conditions, and remain above 10^12 Ohm-cm after 168 hours of water immersion.
Part 3, Section 2 specifies five hot-curing thermal classes: Class 130 (Class B), Class 155 (Class F), Class 180 (Class H), Class 200, and Class 220 based on long-term thermal endurance index limits.
